newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares close weaker as blue chips slide.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares close weaker as blue chips slide.

text.p: Blue chip frirms continued to slide on the Nigerian stock exchange on Tuesday as investors persisted in offloading their stock, dealers said.
The all-share index closed at 8480.08 from 8509.32 on Monday.
Key stocks in major sectors were caught in the plunge as a worsening economic outlook in Nigeria forced investors to avoid long-term investments, dealers said.
"Many fear that the fuel scarcity which has lingered for more than a month and led to escalating production costs will translate to increases in the prices of goods and services," said one trader.
Conglomerates PZ Industries PZIN.LG fell to 28.50 naira, down 30 kobo, and Lever Brothers was 28.00 naira, down 40 kobo. UAC finished 10 kobo lower at 16.50 naira.
In the food sector, Coca-Cola bottler Nigerian Bottling Company lost 40 kobo at 54.50 naira while Cadbury shed 10 kobo at 36.00 naira.
Afribank went down by 33 kobo to close at 6.57 naira. First Bank slid three kobo to 13.40 naira and Union Bank closed 20 kobo down at 11.20 naira.

There was no respite for the leading cement and brewing concerns as West African Portland Cement Company (WAPCO) finished five kobo down at 62.40 naira while Nigerian Breweries fell by the same margin to 18.90 naira.
In the oil marketing sector Agip and Unipetrol fell to 18.30 naira and 68.00 naira, losing 20 and 15 kobo respectively.
Nestle was the big gainer, closing 60 kobo higher at 49.70 naira.

Hospital group Ekocorp which said its recently-acquired scanning equipment would enhance its earnings rose five kobo to 4.90 naira and agricultural firm Okomu Oil palm chalked up two kobo to 12.80 naira.
